precepts.text: Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear than to give the sacrifice of fools. Some come into the sanctuary with pride and contention, thinking they know much when they do not; keep your foot means keep your mouth shut and hear, the same charge God gave Moses at the bush.
precepts.point: God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
At the bush God told Moses, “Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.” The Most High expects humility, that we humble ourselves before him. Moses was a great man in Egypt, second to Pharaoh, raised in all the customs of Egypt, and God said, I don't want to hear all of that. The shoes were symbolic.

Ecclesiastes 5:1 is what the Most High requires: “Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and be more ready to hear, than to give the sacrifice of fools: for they consider not that they do evil.” A lot of times we come with pride and contention, acting like we know. You don't know a damn thing, because if you did, you would not have followed white Jesus.

Our brothers and sisters in the world do not consider that they are in evil, and a lot of times when they come into the sanctuaries it is the same thing: pride, contention, thinking they know much when they do not. Keep thy foot means keep your mouth shut when you enter the house of God and be ready to hear, the same thing he told Moses.

The same is required of us coming into this truth. All the Christian garbage we learned, leave it outside. Islam, garbage, leave it outside. Nuwaubianism, Afrocentric, black power: all garbage. We must reform our minds as Israelites and meditate in these scriptures.

precepts.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, before Abraham was, I am. That is who spoke to Moses out of the bush: Christ.
precepts.point: God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Moses asked what name to give the children of Israel, and “God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” So who was speaking to Moses out of the bush? You should already know: Christ.

John 8:58 proves it: “Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” Before Abraham was, I am. The same I AM who sent Moses to Pharaoh is Christ, speaking before Abraham ever lived. It was Christ who spoke directly to Moses.

That is why Moses could teach the gospel in the wilderness. Christ held him up on the mountain for a long season, forty days and forty nights, and showed him the secrets of the times, the beginning, the middle and the end. The God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob who came down to deliver us out of Egypt is the anointed.

precepts.text: I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name JEHOVAH was I not known to them.
precepts.point: The elders taught Yahawah and there was no secret meeting to stop saying it; say it in prayer if you want to, there is no sin in it. The problem is telling people they are not saved if they do not, while they break every law under the sun.

precepts.text: There appeared to Moses in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush; him did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
Stephen recounts the bush. “And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.” Moses drew near, “the voice of the Lord came unto him, Saying, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”, and “Put off thy shoes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest is holy ground.” It is the same account as Exodus 3, the angel in the flame and the voice of the Lord out of the bush.

Then Stephen tells who that angel was to Moses: “This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.” The angel which appeared in the bush is the one who sent Moses to deliver Israel and brought them out “after that he had shewed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.”

Precept upon precept with Joshua 5 and Hebrews 2, this identifies the angel of the Lord in the burning bush: it was Christ.

precepts.text: This is that Moses which said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; he was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.” That prophet is Christ.

“This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina, and with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us”. The angel which spake to Moses in the mount Sina, at the bush and in the church in the wilderness, is the same angel by whose hand Moses was sent as a ruler and a deliverer. Moses received the lively oracles from that angel: the angel in the burning bush was Christ.

precepts.text: The captain of the host of the LORD said to Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy; the same command given at the bush.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
At the bush the voice said, “put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.” When Joshua was by Jericho, “there stood a man over against him with his sword drawn in his hand”, who said, “as captain of the host of the Lord am I now come.” Joshua fell on his face and worshipped, and “the captain of the Lord’s host said unto Joshua, Loose thy shoe from off thy foot; for the place whereon thou standest is holy.”

It is the same command that was given at the bush, from the same one. The captain of the host of the Lord is the angel that appeared to Moses in the flame of fire, and Hebrews 2 names the captain: Christ.

precepts.text: Jesus was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, the captain of their salvation made perfect through sufferings; the captain of the Lord's host is Christ.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels for the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honour; that he by the grace of God should taste death for every man.” The Father, “in bringing many sons unto glory”, made “the captain of their salvation perfect through sufferings.”

The captain of their salvation is Jesus Christ. The captain of the host of the Lord who told Joshua to loose his shoe is that captain, and he gave Joshua the very command given to Moses at the bush. Precept upon precept, the angel of the Lord in the burning bush was Christ.

precepts.text: Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way; obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
The same angel that appeared in the bush went before Israel out of Egypt. “Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.”

My name is in him: the Most High's name is in that Angel, which is why the voice out of the bush could say, “I am the God of thy father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” If Israel obeyed his voice, the Lord would be “an enemy unto thine enemies”, and “mine Angel shall go before thee, and bring thee in unto the Amorites, and the Hittites, and the Perizzites, and the Canaanites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites: and I will cut them off.” That Angel, by whose hand Moses was sent as a ruler and a deliverer, is Christ.

precepts.text: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
precepts.point: Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.” The one Moses met at the bush is not flesh of this earth.

Yet God being a Spirit does not mean He has no body. He has a celestial, angelic body, as 1 Corinthians 15 and Daniel 7 show, which is how man could be made in His image, and which is why Moses “hid his face; for he was afraid to look upon God.”

precepts.text: There are celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial; the Most High has an angelic celestial body.
precepts.point: Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“All flesh is not the same flesh: but there is one kind of flesh of men, another flesh of beasts, another of fishes, and another of birds. There are also celestial bodies, and bodies terrestrial: but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another.”

God is a Spirit, but He has a body: a celestial, angelic body, not flesh of this earth. That is how the angel of the Lord could appear to Moses in a flame of fire out of the midst of the bush, and how man could be made in His image.

precepts.text: The Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool; He has form and body, not of this earth.
precepts.point: Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.”

The Ancient of days has a garment and the hair of his head like the pure wool. He has form and body, celestial and not of this earth; that is how man could be made in His image. Moses hid his face at the bush because he was afraid to look upon God, who has a face to look upon.

precepts.text: He took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham, and in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren.
precepts.point: Christ was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. He took not on him the nature of angels, but the seed of Abraham, made like unto his brethren, born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
Christ was the angel in the bush, but he was not reincarnated when he came in the flesh. “For verily he took not on him the nature of angels; but he took on him the seed of Abraham.”

“Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto his brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things pertaining to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.” He was born a man so that he could die for the nation of Israel, for an angel cannot die. The God of Abraham, of Isaac and of Jacob who spoke out of the bush took on the seed of Abraham to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.

precepts.text: Jesus said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am; Christ identified himself with the I AM of the bush.
precepts.point: Christ spoke to that very name: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am. He was telling them he was the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob who met Moses at the bush.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
God told Moses His name: “I AM THAT I AM: and he said, Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you.” The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob: “this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.”

Christ spoke to that very name: “Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.” He was telling them that he was the I AM, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob who met Moses at the bush.

precepts.text: The children of Israel borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment; and the LORD gave the people favour, so that they lent unto them such things as they required: and they spoiled the Egyptians.
precepts.point: It happened exactly the way it was spoken: after the firstborn of Egypt were slain, the Egyptians lent Israel what they required, and they spoiled the Egyptians.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
At the bush the Lord promised: “I will give this people favour in the sight of the Egyptians: and it shall come to pass, that, when ye go, ye shall not go empty”. Every woman would borrow of her neighbour jewels of silver, jewels of gold and raiment, “and ye shall spoil the Egyptians.”

It happened exactly the way it was spoken. After the firstborn of Egypt were slain, “the children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they borrowed of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and raiment: And the Lord gave the people favour in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they lent unto them such things as they required. And they spoiled the Egyptians.”

precepts.text: Put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground; Moses knew all the ways and deities of the Egyptians, and he was told to be quiet, humble himself, and receive the milk of the laws so he could grow.
precepts.point: Why worship what the Most High created to serve you? The sun, moon, and stars are ordinances that keep their order and do their job, which is why the new moon can be kept; Israel is the one out of order when the commandments are not kept.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“Draw not nigh hither: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.”

Moses knew all the ways and deities of the Egyptians, the beasts, fowls, creeping things and fish they deified, and the sun, the moon and the stars they worshipped. And he was told to be quiet, humble himself, and receive the milk of the laws so he could grow.

That is the posture for coming out of the idols of Egypt: what was learned in that land is filth, and it is put off at the door like the shoes from off the feet, for the place is holy ground.

precepts.text: I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows.
precepts.point: When the judge was dead, they returned and corrupted themselves more than their fathers, ceasing not from their own doings nor from their stubborn way. As soon as we got out of the condition we were in, we went right back to doing the same thing again, because this is a rebellious and stubborn people, even to this very day.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“for it repented the Lord because of their groanings by reason of them that oppressed them and vexed them.” It was the same in Egypt: “I have surely seen the affliction of my people which are in Egypt, and have heard their cry by reason of their taskmasters; for I know their sorrows”. The Most High hears Israel’s groanings under the oppressor, in Egypt and in the days of the judges alike, and it moves him to raise up deliverers.

He does not want to see us on the bottom. But we trespassed against his commandments, so we have to be punished for it; and when the judge was dead, we went right back to doing the same thing again.

precepts.text: Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian, and led the flock to the mountain of God, where the Most High called him out of the midst of the bush.
precepts.point: Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High; he took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
David was not the first. “Now Moses kept the flock of Jethro his father in law, the priest of Midian: and he led the flock to the backside of the desert, and came to the mountain of God, even to Horeb.” There the Most High called him out of the midst of the bush.

Moses was following a literal flock when he was called, just as David was keeping his father’s sheep.

precepts.text: Moses was called from the flock of animals to bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt, and he ended up feeding them with the laws of the Most High.
precepts.point: Taking a keeper of sheep and making him the shepherd of the nation is a pattern with the Most High; he took leaders and prophets from following literal flocks and set them to feed the flock of Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 16: The Lord Looketh on the Heart

precepts.why:
At the bush the Most High said, “Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh, that thou mayest bring forth my people the children of Israel out of Egypt.” Moses was called from the flock of animals to bring forth the children of Israel out of Egypt, and he ended up feeding them with the laws of the Most High.

That is the same pattern as David: the keeper of a flock made the shepherd of the nation.

precepts.text: This is His name forever and His memorial unto all generations: the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
precepts.point: But the Most High shall endure forever and His remembrance unto all generations. That remembrance is that He is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

note.label: Psalm 102: Hear My Prayer, O Lord

precepts.why:
“But thou, O Lord, shalt endure for ever; and thy remembrance unto all generations.” Man's days are like a shadow that declines, withered like grass, but the Most High endures forever. That remembrance is that he is the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

He said so to Moses: “Thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath sent me unto you: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.” This is his name forever and his memorial unto all generations: the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

The remembrance unto all generations in Psalm 102 is the memorial unto all generations in Exodus 3. The Most High endures forever as the God of our fathers.
